title: Trajan conquers Dacia
description: Roman legions take the Dacian capital and King Decebalus kills himself, and Dacia becomes a Roman province.

title: Rome gives up Dacia
description: Emperor Aurelian withdraws the army and administration from Dacia to the south bank of the Danube, ending about 165 years of Roman rule.

title: Battle of Posada
description: Basarab I of Wallachia ambushes the army of Charles I of Hungary in a mountain pass, which secures the independence of the principality.

title: Founding of Moldavia
description: Bogdan of Cuhea crosses the Carpathians from Maramureș and takes Moldavia out of Hungarian control, founding the principality.

title: Bobâlna revolt
description: Hungarian and Romanian peasants rise in Transylvania, and the nobles, Székelys and Saxons answer with the Union of the Three Nations, which shapes Transylvanian politics for centuries.

title: Night attack at Târgoviște
description: Vlad the Impaler raids the camp of Sultan Mehmed II at night in an attempt to kill him during the Ottoman invasion of Wallachia.

title: Battle of Vaslui
description: Stephen the Great of Moldavia defeats a much larger Ottoman army, one of the heaviest Ottoman defeats of the century.

title: Michael the Brave unites the three principalities
description: After taking Transylvania and Moldavia, the prince of Wallachia briefly rules all three lands, later seen as a forerunner of modern Romania.

title: Bucharest Bible printed
description: The first complete Bible in Romanian is printed under Prince Șerban Cantacuzino, a landmark in the written language.

title: Battle of Stănilești
description: An Ottoman army surrounds Peter the Great and his Moldavian ally Dimitrie Cantemir, after which the sultan replaces native princes with Phanariot Greeks.

title: Revolt of Horea, Cloșca and Crișan
description: Romanian serfs in Transylvania rise against the nobility, and although the revolt is put down Joseph II abolishes personal serfdom there the next year.

title: Treaty of Bucharest
description: At the end of a Russo-Turkish war the Ottoman Empire cedes the eastern half of Moldavia, Bessarabia, to Russia.

title: Wallachian uprising
description: Tudor Vladimirescu raises Oltenia against the Phanariot regime, and after the revolt the Ottomans return the thrones of Wallachia and Moldavia to native princes.

title: Proclamation of Islaz
description: Wallachian revolutionaries announce a programme of civil rights and land reform and form a provisional government, which Ottoman and Russian troops remove in September.

title: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia
description: The Wallachian assembly elects Alexandru Ioan Cuza, already chosen in Moldavia, as its prince, joining the two principalities in the state that becomes Romania.

title: Carol I becomes prince
description: After Cuza is forced out, Karl of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen is installed as ruling prince and a constitution on the Belgian model is adopted.

title: Independence declared
description: Parliament declares Romania independent of the Ottoman Empire, and the Romanian army then fights beside Russia at Plevna.

title: Kingdom of Romania proclaimed
description: Parliament raises the country to a kingdom and Carol I is crowned its first king.

title: Peasants' revolt
description: A revolt against the land-lease system spreads from northern Moldavia across the country and is put down by the army with thousands of deaths.

title: Battle of Mărășești
description: The rebuilt Romanian army, with Russian support, stops a German and Austro-Hungarian offensive aimed at occupying what was left of the country.

title: Great Union
description: An assembly of Romanians of Transylvania votes for union with Romania, completing a state that has also gained Bessarabia and Bukovina, and the day is now the national holiday.

title: Soviet Union takes Bessarabia
description: After a Soviet ultimatum Romania gives up Bessarabia and northern Bukovina, the first of the territorial losses of that summer.

title: Iași pogrom
description: Romanian authorities, soldiers and civilians, with German troops, kill more than 13,000 Jews in the city and on sealed trains leaving it.

title: King Michael's coup
description: King Michael has Marshal Antonescu arrested and takes Romania out of the Axis and over to the Allied side as the Red Army enters the country.

title: King Michael abdicates
description: The communist government forces the king to abdicate and proclaims a people's republic the same day.

title: Ceaușescu condemns the invasion of Czechoslovakia
description: Nicolae Ceaușescu publicly denounces the Warsaw Pact invasion, which wins him popularity at home and credit in the West.

title: Vrancea earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 7.2 kills about 1,500 people in Romania, most of them in Bucharest.

title: Brașov rebellion
description: Workers of the Red Flag truck plant march on the party headquarters over pay and shortages, the largest protest against Ceaușescu before 1989.

title: Revolution begins in Timișoara
description: Protests against the eviction of pastor László Tőkés turn into a revolt against the regime that spreads to Bucharest within a week.

title: Ceaușescu executed
description: Nicolae and Elena Ceaușescu are tried by a military tribunal and shot, ending the only violent overthrow of a communist government in Europe in 1989.

title: Mineriad of June 1990
description: Miners brought to the capital by the new government attack anti-government protesters and opposition offices.

title: Romania joins the European Union
description: Romania becomes a member of the European Union, three years after joining NATO.
